notes: The registered pardon row is POS_DEAD at level 1, then the handler applies its own LVL_IMMORT/PLR_CHOSEN gate (R1/R2/R5e).
An ordinary level-1 non-chosen caller receives the exact Huh?!? inner authorization response before argument parsing (R1/R2/R3/R5e).
A low-level caller carrying PLR_CHOSEN is admitted through the C inner guard and can reach the pardon switch (R1/R5e).
An authorized caller with no target receives Yes, but for whom?!? (R1/R3/R5e).
A missing visible-world player reaches the exact There is no such player. response (R1/R3/R5e).
A visible trainee mob is rejected before SCMD_PARDON with C's exact mob response (R1/R3/R5e).
A target above both the actor and LVL_IMMORT is refused without flag mutation (R1/R5e).
An already unflagged target emits Your victim is not flagged. and returns before save or success bytes (R1/R3/R5e).
A flagged target produces the exact Pardoned. acknowledgement to the actor (R1/R3/R5e).
The remote target receives You have been pardoned by the Gods! through the victim descriptor (R1/R3/R5e).
C one_argument skips the leading fill word and ignores trailing words; the full argument remainder is preserved to the existing parser (R1/R2/R3/R5e).
Global visible-player lookup resolves the lower-case target spelling exactly as C str_cmp/get_player_vis does (R1/R3/R5e).
The C self alias resolves the actor; actor and victim sends therefore concatenate both success messages on one descriptor (R1/R2/R3/R5e).
The shared visible world target resolution, NPC rejection, and higher-immortal guard are already owned by the do_wizutil mute boundary; this slice proves pardon's call boundary and switch (R5b/R5c).
